key_insight: OpenGEM26 expands molecular ML training data with 4.4 million DFT conformations, enabling a graph neural network force field (GPTFF-mol) that better captures energies and forces for diverse organic molecules.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical surrogate for DFT in atomistic simulations, especially for sulfur- and chlorine-containing organic systems where accurate but efficient force fields are needed.
method: Built OpenGEM26 from 200,000 unique molecules and 4.4 million conformations.
Computed optimized trajectories and non-equilibrium structures at ωB97X-D/Def2-SVP and Def2-TZVP with dispersion corrections.
Trained GPTFF-mol as a graph neural network potential for energies and forces.
evidence_signal: The model reports 16 meV/molecule energy MAE (0.82 meV/atom) and outperforms ANI-2x on force prediction, with validation on butane rotation and keto-enol tautomerization.
watch_item: Performance may depend on coverage of the chemical space and the level of theory used, so transfer to larger molecules or chemistries outside H/C/N/O/S/Cl should be checked carefully.
paper_title: Graph Neural Network Force Fields (GPTFF-mol) for Organic Molecules from Optimization Trajectories (OpenGEM26)
